key_factors: District's R+19 partisan lean gives Republicans a large structural edge even with the seat open
Chris Stigall has out-raised Josh Smead roughly seven to one and holds a wide cash advantage

model.rationale: The district's nineteen-point Republican lean survives Sam Graves's retirement, and Stigall's fundraising dominance leaves Smead without the resources to compete; fundamentals and market pricing point the same way.
model.watch: A scandal involving the Republican nominee or a wave of late outside Democratic spending would be the main way this moves, though the required swing is very large.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

Open seat: Sam Graves (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Missouri's Sixth District in the state's northwest has been a reliably Republican seat, and Sam Graves's retirement does not put that advantage on the ballot. The district's partisan lean of roughly nineteen points Republican gives the GOP nominee a large structural head start, and the national environment offers Democrats little offset.

Republican Chris Stigall has raised nearly a million dollars, about seven and a half times Democrat Josh Smead's total, and holds a wide cash-on-hand advantage. No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and fundraising. Prediction markets price the Republican at roughly ninety-five percent. A Libertarian candidate appears on the ballot but shows no measurable support. The seat remains firmly in Republican hands barring an unexpected shift.
